counter_evidence:
The claim holds for pytest. It fails in three other places, each backed by positive evidence from code installed in this repo or from the design itself.

(1) Jest 29.7.0 has no phase field, so a hook crash looks exactly like a test-body failure. Files are in technician-app/node_modules/jest-circus/build.
- eventHandler.js:164-185 (case 'hook_failure') pushes a beforeEach or afterEach error into the same `test.errors` array that test_fn_failure uses (:213-217).
- A beforeAll error is copied onto every test in the describe block (utils.js:444, addErrorToEachTestUnderDescribe).
- run.js:312 then skips the test function: "We don't run the test if there's already an error in before hooks."
- The --json assertionResult (legacy-code-todo-rewrite/jestAdapterInit.js:127-160) has only these fields: ancestorTitles, duration, failureDetails, failureMessages, fullName, invocations, location, numPassingAsserts, retryReasons, status, title.
- `invocations` is incremented at test_start, before any hook runs.
- Result: a hook that throws a message matching present_when is reported as `status: "failed"` on the named id, even though the test body never ran. That is PRESENT, then applies. The artifact cannot express "setup error => inconclusive" or "the executed test id".

(2) Jest also misattributes async errors. eventHandler.js:265-276 (case 'error') attaches any uncaughtException or unhandledRejection to `state.currentlyRunningTest`. The maintainers' own comment says this "will result in one test's error failing another test". So a leaked async throw that matches the template can turn the named test PRESENT.

(3) Vitest 4.1.9 has the same problem for per-test hooks. In node_modules/@vitest/runner/dist/chunk-artifact.js:2940-2981, beforeEach (:2947), the test callback, onTaskFinished, afterEach and fixture cleanup all funnel into failTask(test.result). The json reporter (node_modules/vitest/dist/chunks/index.UpGiHP7g.js:3573) then emits status "failed" with failureMessages and no phase. Only beforeAll is safe: :3135-3138 calls markTasksAsSkipped.

(4) A regex_in_span presence probe can match a comment on a fixed tree.
- The adopted spec (KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:255; architect-A check_kinds) says only "PRESENT when the pattern occurs inside". Proposal C's comment exclusion was not adopted.
- This repo writes the forbidden construct into comments inside the fixed gate spans. At a31924a: backend/app/features/ops/deps.py:42-43, customer_messaging/router.py:154-155 and service.py:155-156 all read "compare_secret, not hmac.compare_digest on str".
- architect-C measured comment matches inverting two naive probes: compare_digest went from 4 to 9 matches, and `catch { return; }` from 0 to 1.
- Control pairs are pinned historical commits, so they catch only a comment already present at passes_at. Take a comment added later inside the span:
  - the span hash changes, so the entry goes suspect;
  - the historical controls still flip, so early cutoff re-stamps the trace;
  - inject-control re-tests only the PRESENT side;
  - the negative-corpus check runs only at write time (sec7).
  HEAD then reads PRESENT, the verdict is applies, and the fix text is released on already-fixed code.

(5) Symptom-shaped templates prove sensitivity, not specificity. ex6's present_when is "assertion on status 429". The test line backend/tests/test_identity_integration.py:99 is `assert locked.status_code == 429, locked.text`, so any call-phase cause of a non-429 status matches. A control pair shows the check can flip between two commits; it does not show that PRESENT on a third tree means the root cause.

What survives (pytest): src/_pytest/junitxml.py (main, fetched) writes <failure> only when `report.when == "call"`. Setup and teardown failures become <error> with the message 'failed on setup/teardown with "..."'. A collection error becomes <error message="collection failure"> on the collector's id. Skip and xfail become <skipped>.

pytest caveats:
- On main, the message attribute passes through shorten_message (MESSAGE_ATTR_BUDGET = 500).
- The element text is the full longrepr, including the test's own source lines.
- A call failure followed by a teardown error produces two <testcase> elements with the same id.
- The XML is written inside the pytest process that loads the target tree's conftest.py. The nonce binds only the probe JSON.
narrowed_claim:
For pytest test_id checks, the verdict can be derived without vacuity or crash-induced applies, under four conditions:
- PRESENT requires a <failure> element (call phase only).
- The present_when template is matched against the reprcrash message: the untruncated first block of the element text, not the source listing.
- A test id that appears more than once (failure plus teardown error) is inconclusive.
- Exit codes 126/127/137/255, pytest exit 5, collection and setup errors, skipped or missing ids, Docker down, a missing anchor and malformed JSON all map to inconclusive.

Jest and Vitest json artifacts carry no phase, and Jest attaches stray async errors to the running test. So jest/vitest checks cannot meet the claim without a runner-owned phase signal; until one exists they can return at most inconclusive. A regex_in_span presence probe can still reach applies through a comment or other non-code text inside the span. A control pair at two historical commits shows the check is sensitive, not that PRESENT on the caller's tree is specific.
design_consequence:
1. Jest and Vitest phase signal.
   - Jest: get the phase from a runner-supplied file the runner passes on the command line. For example, a custom testEnvironment overlaid into the tmpfs whose handleTestEvent records test_fn_start, test_fn_failure and hook_failure with the nonce into a runner JSON.
   - Vitest: a runner-supplied reporter or setup file doing the same.
   - Both: PRESENT requires a test_fn_failure on the named id, exactly one failure message, and no uncaught-error attribution during that test.
   - Until this is built, cap jest/vitest checks at inconclusive (or limit them to hook-free test files verified statically, run alone with -t and --runInBand).
   - ex5's completionPrefill check happens to be hook-free. Most outbox and attendance tests use beforeEach.

2. regex_in_span and ordered_in_span.
   - Match only code tokens: strip comments and strings per language, or reuse C's non-comment-line rule.
   - A matched anchor must be unique; an ambiguous anchor returns inconclusive.
   - Add a required specificity control on the ABSENT side: passes_at plus a stored mutant that injects the pattern as a comment must still read ABSENT. For test checks, passes_at plus a hook throwing the template message must read inconclusive.

3. pytest.
   - Match against the reprcrash message, not the full element text.
   - Refuse duplicate testcase elements for one id.
   - Require templates to name the root-cause signature (exception class plus message, or the observed status pair such as "assert 200 == 429"), never a bare expected value.
   - Record that the junit XML is written by a process that loads the target tree's conftest.py. Refuse a run whose target conftest defines pytest_runtest_makereport or junit hooks, or treat that run as inconclusive.

4. Fault-injection list for the gate phases at KNOWLEDGE-STORE-DESIGN-2026-11.md:564 and :597. Add these, each expected inconclusive (or ABSENT for the comment mutant):
   - a Jest beforeEach throwing the template message;
   - a Jest beforeAll throwing it;
   - a Vitest beforeEach throwing it;
   - an afterEach-only failure;
   - a leaked setTimeout throw from a sibling test;
   - a pytest call failure followed by a teardown error;
   - a comment containing the pattern inside the span at HEAD.
